items.title: We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite.
items.summary: Video showing the Project Suncatcher team explaining the project and reacting to the TPU-generated haiku
items.excerpt:
Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence

On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher. The launch marked the first step in our long-term research moonshot to explore powering AI compute in space. Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests. This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit.

During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success:

Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨

Following this initial output, we tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts reporting the technical status of the payload systems. Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027. Our chips have officially earned their space wings — an important achievement on the long road ahead for this cosmic moonshot.

items.excerpt:
Utility-scale solar developers are increasingly co-locating battery storage with new solar photovoltaic capacity. As of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017, according to data reported to EIA by operators.

Reported plans for solar additions scheduled to come online in the last three months of this year show that the share with co-located battery storage could increase to 19% this year. Longer-term plans indicate that this trend will continue, with the portion increasing to more than 30% in plans submitted for 2027 and 2028.

When operators co-locate battery storage with solar, they can direct solar electricity output to the grid or to the battery, depending on the wholesale prices. Wholesale prices in regions with large solar participation tend to fall when solar contributions are high and rise as they decrease. Plants with both solar and battery storage can manage the combined output of their generating resources to maximize their value in a changing wholesale price environment.

The goal of the partnership is to help people who are blind, Deafblind or have low vision explore the possibilities of AI wearable technology, and draw on the knowledge, expertise and lived experience of the community to shape a more accessible future.

Funding from Meta will support CNIB in four areas:

Along with funding to help advance inclusive innovation, Meta is donating AI glasses through CNIB Come to Work program, which will put tools into the hands of people exploring employment opportunities and building their careers. The program provides training and practical resources to help participants assess how wearable technology can assist them in securing employment, succeeding at work and pursuing their goals.

People use Meta’s AI glasses for everything from listening to music, to live translation and hands-free calls. The real kicker is that understanding usually already exists in the form of a semantic model in a Looker, dbt, Snowflake, Databricks, or SAP system. But because each definition stays locked inside its own tool, every agent guesses at it… and often gets it wrong.

Enterprise organizations often leverage multiple data platforms, including Databricks, to execute heavy Apache Spark jobs alongside BigQuery to power highly concurrent analytics workloads. Historically, bridging these systems often meant building complex pipelines to copy data between environments. This approach increases storage costs, introduces latency, and fragments security controls.

With Google Cloud’s borderless Lakehouse, you can now query Databricks-managed Apache Iceberg tables straight from BigQuery. This zero-copy approach removes the need to duplicate data: BigQuery reads the same files Databricks writes, and new changes appear after Lakehouse's next scheduled metadata refresh (as often as every 5 minutes).

Managed Iceberg tables automatically generates Iceberg-compatible metadata alongside native Delta logs. Data engineering teams can store Parquet files once in Google Cloud Storage (GCS) using Databricks. Rather than loading this information into BigQuery, Lakehouse reads the Iceberg metadata directly, applying BigQuery’s vectorized engine directly to open-format files in GCS.

Colombia is importing more liquefied natural gas (LNG) as domestic production continues to fall. A potential drought this fall and winter could limit the availability of hydroelectric generation and boost the country’s demand for natural gas power generation. Colombia’s government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought resulting from an expected strong El Niño.

Average annual marketed natural gas production in Colombia decreased from 1,070 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) in 2022 to 772 MMcf/d in 2025, according to Gestor del Mercado de Gas Natural en Columbia (BEC). Between January and August 2026, production declined further, averaging 673 MMcf/d. The fields that produce most of Colombia’s natural gas—specifically Cusiana, Cupiagua, Pauto Sur, and the offshore Guajira fields—have been declining since 2022, with no large discoveries developed to replace them. Proved reserves fell 39% to 1.7 trillion cubic feet between 2022 and 2025, according to the National Hydrocarbons Agency.

As production declined, LNG imports grew. LNG imports accounted for a record 31% of Colombia’s monthly natural gas supply in July 2026, according to data from BEC, Colombia’s gas market administrator.

items.excerpt:
AI doesn’t wait. The foundations of every industry are already cracking. This isn’t a story about one sector. Manufacturing. Finance. Healthcare. Data centers. The entire industrial order is being rebuilt around AI — and it’s happening now. Knowing about AI is no longer a competitive advantage. You need to see through it. That’s why our Newsroom is putting AI — and the semiconductors that power it — under the microscope.

In [Tech Note], Professor Younghyun Kim of the School of Semiconductor Convergence Engineering at Hanyang University ERICA breaks down data bottlenecks in AI factories and explores silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (CPO) as next-generation technologies that could help overcome them.

The competitiveness of AI semiconductors is no longer determined solely by the processing speed of individual compute chips. The performance of an entire AI factory depends on where data resides, the paths it takes, and how quickly it reaches its destination. In the AI era, the data highway is shifting from electrical signals to light.

Imagine a vast industrial complex filled with hundreds of factories, each equipped with state-of-the-art machinery capable of producing goods in the blink of an eye. But what happens if the roads connecting these factories have only one lane in each direction? Having visibility into your network traffic is essential to operating Kubernetes environments effectively. When a service slows down or loses connectivity, knowing who is talking to whom lets you narrow the problem down quickly. In a standard cloud network, flow logs provide that view by recording connections between IP addresses, ports, and protocols. In Kubernetes, however, pods are temporary. Their IP addresses change constantly as pods scale, crash, or move between nodes, so a raw log entry showing 10.4.2.18 talking to 10.4.8.44 tells you little about which workload (and pod) owned that address, what namespace it was in, or what application it was trying to reach. By the time you search your cluster, the pod may already be gone!

In a Google Cloud environment, VPC Flow Logs closes this gap at the network layer. Google Cloud's virtual network already sees every connection a pod makes, so each sampled flow is recorded with the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) metadata behind the IP address: pod, workload, namespace, and service. You get workload-level attribution for L3/L4 traffic without deploying extra agents or sidecars, and it complements in-cluster Container Network Interface (CNI) and dataplane observability tools you may already run when you need deeper detail. Let’s take a deeper look at how VPC Flow Logs and GKE work together, and how to get started with it.

On October 26, 2026, Broadcom Inc. (the “Company”) arranged for financial partners to take on a portion of certain agreements to purchase AI racks based on custom AI accelerators designed by the Company and the related lease agreements with the Company’s customer that enable the deployment of compute capacity.

In connection with this arrangement, the Company is providing residual value support to a newly formed special purpose vehicle (the “Backstop”). The Backstop is a contingent liability the Company believes has a low probability of occurring, supported by the expectation of a strong profitability trajectory of the customer and the sustaining value of the underlying assets. The total amount of the Backstop increases as the AI racks are delivered and deployed and decreases as the customer makes payments on its lease obligations.

In the event of a lease default by the customer, the remedies to limit the Company’s liability exposure include the assumption of the applicable lease, reselling the AI racks back to the seller at a fixed price under certain conditions, or arranging a sale of the applicable AI racks. The Company’s potential liability under the Backstop will be equal to any difference between 72.5% of the outstanding amounts owed on the lease and the value of the AI racks received upon the sale of the assets at that time. The Company’s maximum potential liability under the Backstop upon the deployment of the AI racks, on an undiscounted basis, is approximately $43 billion.

Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry.

Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver.

Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation.

The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.

With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters. Every world also generates native audio on the fly, including ambient sounds, music, and interactive dialogue.

Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing.

We have started rolling out Genie 4 to a limited group of trusted testers. It’s coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog.

Using this functionality reduces the administrative overhead of maintaining least-privilege security and agent governance, while maximizing utility, and accelerating deployment.

As AI workloads scale across every industry, organizations need compute options that optimize throughput, latency, and unit economics across the AI lifecycle. To meet this demand, Oracle and Google Cloud are partnering to bring Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), making OCI the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs. Together, we will deploy TPU capacity on OCI starting in the calendar year 2027.

Google built its first TPU more than ten years ago on a clear product thesis: co-designing custom silicon alongside optical networking, power delivery, liquid cooling, and compiler software yields gains in performance per watt and total cost of ownership that isolated components cannot match.

TPU v1 delivered 30x the throughput per watt of contemporary processors. Today, TPUs train and serve Gemini across Google's billion-user products, and the eighth-generation TPUs deliver up to 12.6 PFLOPS of native FP4 compute per chip, over 100x TPU v1's 92 TFLOPS at up to 2x the performance per watt of the previous generation. However, raw FLOPS alone do not determine customer economics across training and inference. For training, the governing metric is goodput; the percentage of time a cluster spends doing productive computation. For inference, the governing metrics are latency and cost per token. TPUs address both through system-level co-design.

This enables robots to converse naturally with humans, orchestrate low-level action models and hardware APIs, execute multi-minute tasks involving hundreds of decisions, and collaborate across multi-robot teams.

Today, we are bringing this same frontier embodied reasoning model to enterprise production environments: Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now available in public preview on the Gemini platform.
